title: MacPrune Mac Cleaner Pro Lifetime Licence 80% off: US$4 (~A$5.76) @ MacPrune
body:
Deal: MacPrune Mac Cleaner Pro Lifetime Licence 80% off: US$4 (~A$5.76) @ MacPrune

[chrism238] How does this compare with the free Pearcleaner?
[sammrjn] it doesn't have proper cleaning option its just better as a complete package
[ringofan] On your site it mentions it’s freeware and:
MacPrune is free. Seriously. No hidden fees, no subscriptions, no upsells.
[sammrjn] it was our typo, the basic free option will always be free like cleaning the cache and all basic stuffs
[Jenbrook] Yeah there is no mention on your site about subscription fees or anything, does this mean if we download it for free we will be subject later to a update that will kill it unless we pay a subscription? if yes then stuff your company that would be dirty rotten.
[sammrjn] It's a one-time payment, free forever, including all future updates/upgrades. No subscription, no rug-pull.
We're still in early access so pricing isn't fully locked on the site yet , once we're past that stage, all new new customers will move to an annual plan going forward. But anyone who buys in now is grandfathered for life on the one-time deal. You have my word on that.
Will get the site updated to make this clearer, thanks for flagging it.
[Jenbrook] Did this guys Ozbargain account get hacked?
[sammrjn] no, not really was just out for a quick coffee and back to desk
[Jenbrook] Please explain where the paid option is on your site? the link Buy Now / Pricing https://macprune.com/pricing has no mention of a paid subscription?
EDIT: Ok I see you just updated your site as previously the pricing link looked like this https://ibb.co/wr4KtMQZ
[sammrjn] thanks for flagging it out,
we have fixed the issues
[Jenbrook] Because I downloaded the app before you changed your website pricing page do I still get features like CPU process monitor & force-quit killer for free as mentioned in the screenshot I posted?
[sammrjn] yes, we haven't changed anything in mac app code base, we are just updating the website for general info,
[stu ped asso] If you’re paying for something it’s not free, right?
Here’s a simple and open sourced tool to keep your Mac tidy for free: https://github.com/tw93/Mole
[sammrjn] I totally agree that many of these things can be done manually if you are technical enough.
But for a fraction of the cost, almost the price of one coffee, MacPrune gives users a clean and simple UI so non-technical people don’t need to touch Terminal, run commands, or worry about deleting the wrong files.
[jv] MacPrune 80% off
Thanks, my Mac Trees have dropped all their Mac Leaves …
[sammrjn] Haha exactly, MacPrune is here to clean up all those fallen MacLeaves
[sammrjn] Thanks, feel free to share your thoughts after its use,
[dangerdanger] Not trying to troll, I'm genuinely curious. I have several Macs, never needed this kind of app. How much good will it do for my Macs?
I never run out of hard drive space, my CPU rarely hangs (can't remember when this last happened).
[sammrjn] This is a common pain point for anyone who watches a lot of YouTube or Netflix, uses Xcode, or does basic development work on a Mac with limited storage like 256GB or 512GB.
Over time, your Mac can build up a lot of cache and temporary files.
Even with normal day-to-day use, you might be surprised how much cache is sitting on your machine.
download and give it a go. It will show you an overview of the cache and storage usage on your Mac, so you can decide what you want to clean.
[hashtagbargain] Can I buy once and use it on all my macs? Or it is per device?
[Ppanthi] I am unable to utilize my second account on the same device. Could you please provide clarification on this matter?
